title: L110 — THE SPIKE THAT CLEANED THE BOOK
voice: You placed your stop exactly where the textbook told you, and the price ran through it by three pips before reversing in the direction you picked.
The spike was not random, because the orders sitting at that level were visible to anyone reading the book.
Every retail stop clustered at the same round number becomes a pool of liquidity that a larger order needs to fill.
The price visits the cluster, fills the waiting order, and reverses before the screen refreshes.
Place your stop where the liquidity has already been taken, not where the crowd still sits. Follow KONGRAVE — the mechanics nobody explains.
